- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is high (e.g., >0.6) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or low (e.g., <0.2) — model is overly cautious, missing upward momentum.
- Lag in correction: model often delays reacting to sentiment shifts — especially when sentiment turns positive, forecast still lags 1–2 periods.
- Mean reversion bias: model overcorrects after sharp moves, assuming price will return to “normal” too quickly, ignoring structural trends.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly sensitive to recent sentiment, leading to overfitting to short-term noise — ignore sentiment spikes >0.8 for 30d horizon.
- When sentiment is volatile (e.g., alternating 0.2–0.8), model averages out extremes — underestimates volatility and misses breakout opportunities.
